title: `toc_tokens` names are not HTML-escaped, unlike the rendered TOC
spec: This is the Python-Markdown library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -q`. I build my own navigation from `md.toc_tokens` and insert each `name` into HTML. Headers containing `<`, `>` or `&` come through unescaped, so the token name disagrees with `md.toc` and is unsafe to insert. ``` md = markdown.Markdown(extensions=['markdown.extensions.toc']) md.convert('# Foo > & bar') md.toc_tokens ``` Expected: ``` [{'level': 1, 'id': 'foo-bar', 'name': 'Foo > & bar', 'children': []}] ``` Actual: ``` [{'level': 1, 'id': 'foo-bar', 'name': 'Foo > & bar', 'children': []}] ``` `md.toc` is already correct (`Foo > & bar`). A header that was written as `&` already gives `Foo & bar` in the tokens, so names are meant to be HTML text. The same applies to a label set with `attr_list`: `# Header 4 { data-toc-label="Foo > Baz" }` (extensions `markdown.extensions.toc` and `markdown.extensions.attr_list`) should give the name `Foo > Baz` but gives `Foo > Baz`. Any token `name` should match the text shown in the HTML TOC: special characters escaped exactly once, with markup in labels still stripped to text.
acceptance: The reported header gives the token name `Foo > & bar`
`data-toc-label` values with special characters are escaped the same way in `toc_tokens`, and labels containing tags still reduce to plain text
